title: On some structural properties of graphs with non-negative resistance curvature
summary: A graph is called resistance nonnegative (RN), respectively resistance positive (RP), if it admits positive edge weights such that all vertex resistance curvatures are nonnegative, respectively positive. In this paper, we study the structure of RN and RP graphs in relation to toughness, traceability, and Cartesian products. First, we disprove a conjecture of Fiedler and answer a question of Devriendt in the negative by constructing, for every $n\ge 11$, an $n$-vertex $1$-tough graph that is not RN.
